{"emails": [{"email_id": "email_email_c44632eee847", "folder": "SENT", "sender": "robert.calloway@keystonemortgage.com", "recipients": ["denise.holloway@keystonemortgage.com"], "subject": "Need support for added conditions on delayed files", "content": "Denise,

I'm getting the same feedback now from both production and ops that three active files were delayed by conditions being added in compliance review that were not lender conditions and, at least from how they're being described to me, appear to go beyond our normal regulatory requirements.

Please send me a file-by-file explanation for the added conditions and the basis for each one. I specifically need to understand:

- what triggered the extra review
- whether each item was required by law, investor guidance, or internal overlay
- why the condition was raised at that stage of the file instead of earlier
- whether the same standard is being applied consistently across similar loans

I also want your view on where we are drawing the line between necessary risk control and process layering. If these are true must-haves, I need that clearly documented. If some are preference or best practice, we need to know that too.

Please get this back to me today if you can. Grace and I need something concrete before this turns into a broader production issue.

Robert", "cc": ["grace.yamamoto@keystonemortgage.com"], "parent_id": null, "attachments": {}, "timestamp": "2026-04-07T22:50:00Z", "is_read": true}, {"email_id": "email_email_5f593911160f", "folder": "SENT", "sender": "keisha.williams@keystonemortgage.com", "recipients": ["robert.calloway@keystonemortgage.com"], "subject": "Compliance delays are starting to cost us closings", "content": "Robert,

I need to escalate something that's getting worse.

Denise's added review asks are pushing files back well beyond lender conditions. I have three loans that have each effectively lost about a week because we're chasing extra documentation late in the process, and none of these were lender-driven issues when the files were otherwise moving.

At this point it feels like we're gold-plating files instead of clearing what is actually required. The production impact is real. Between delayed closings, repricing risk, and commissions slipping, this is costing revenue.

content.content: {"result":"{\"emails\": [{\"email_id\": \"email_email_d14e4d3e1586\", \"folder\": \"INBOX\", \"sender\": \"destiny.pham@gmail.com\", \"recipients\": [\"amy.chen@keystonemortgage.com\"], \"subject\": \"This is unacceptable\", \"content\": \"Amy,\\n\\nI am beyond furious right now. Keystone closed my loan, then somehow my mortgage got transferred and nobody made that clear to me. I sent my payment to the company I had been paying, it was returned, and now I find out I was marked 30 days late with the new servicer.\\n\\nThis has hit my credit and I am the one dealing with the consequences for a mess I did not create. I never saw any clear notice from anyone at Keystone that I needed to start paying someone else. A returned payment should have triggered someone to contact me before this turned into a missed payment and credit damage.\\n\\nI need someone at Keystone to explain how this happened and what you are going to do to fix it. This is seriously affecting me and I am not going to just let it go.\\n\\nDestiny Pham\", \"cc\": [\"jasmine.brooks@keystonemortgage.com\"], \"parent_id\": null, \"attachments\": {}, \"timestamp\": \"2026-05-31T21:25:33Z\", \"is_read\": false}, {\"email_id\": \"email_email_5f7b4e360962\", \"folder\": \"INBOX\", \"sender\": \"destiny.pham@gmail.com\", \"recipients\": [\"destiny.pham@gmail.com\"], \"subject\": \"New alert: change detected on your credit report\", \"content\": \"Hi Destiny,\\n\\nWe detected a new change on your credit report today.\\n\\nCreditor: New Horizon Loan Servicing\\nChange detected: 30-day late payment reported\\nAccount status: Past due\\n\\nIf you believe this is inaccurate, contact the creditor directly.\\n\\nCredit Monitoring Team\", \"cc\": [], \"parent_id\": null, \"attachments\": {}, \"timestamp\": \"2026-05-31T19:25:33Z\", \"is_read\": false}, {\"email_id\": \"email_email_d445075dec4a\", \"folder\": \"INBOX\", \"sender\": \"derek.moss@keystonemortgage.com\", \"recipients\": [\"danielle.harrison@gmail.com\"], \"subject\": \"Re: Why is my payment suddenly $400 higher?\", \"content\": \"Danielle,\\n\\nI pulled your closing file and the escrow estimate used for your payment at closing was based on the Mecklenburg County property tax information available at that time. The change showing up now appears to be from a county reassessment that happened after your loan closed, which increased the tax amount your servicer now has to collect through escrow.\\n\\nI'm reviewing the original figures against the updated escrow analysis so I can lay it out clearly for you.\", \"cc\": [], \"parent_id\": null, \"attachments\": {}, \"timestamp\": \"2026-05-26T06:02:33Z\", \"is_read\": false}, {\"email_id\": \"email_email_88be07b6edbc\", \"folder\": \"INBOX\", \"sender\": \"destiny.pham@gmail.com\", \"recipients\": [\"destiny.pham@gmail.com\"], \"subject\": \"Payment returned - account transferred\", \"content\": \"Destiny,\\n\\nWe received your recent mortgage payment, but we are unable to apply it because your loan servicing has transferred to a new servicer.\\n\\nYour payment has been returned. Please refer to the transfer notice previously sent for instructions on where to send future payments.\\n\\nIf you need assistance, contact customer service at the number on your prior statement.\\n\\nHomestead Loan Servicing\", \"cc\": [], \"parent_id\": null, \"attachments\": {}, \"timestamp\": \"2026-05-23T19:28:33Z\", \"is_read\": false}, {\"email_id\": \"email_email_d7931a38613a\", \"folder\": \"INBOX\", \"sender\": \"destiny.pham@gmail.com\", \"recipients\": [\"destiny.pham@gmail.com\"], \"subject\": \"Important: Your mortgage servicing has transferred\", \"content\": \"Hi Destiny,\\n\\nWe recently mailed and emailed notice that effective 5/1, HarborView Loan Servicing is now the servicer for your mortgage loan. Please begin sending all future payments to HarborView starting with your May payment.\\n\\nYour prior servicer will no longer accept payments after the transfer date. If you use online bill pay or autopay, please update it right away.\\n\\nQuestions? Call Customer Care at (800) 364-0148.\\n\\nHarborView Loan Servicing\", \"cc\": [], \"parent_id\": null, \"attachments\": {}, \"timestamp\": \"2026-04-29T19:25:33Z\", \"is_read\": false}, {\"email_id\": \"email_email_df47bddbe56d\", \"folder\": \"INBOX\", \"sender\": \"megan.ellis@homesteadwholesale.com\", \"recipients\": [\"elena.marchetti@keystonemortgage.com\"], \"subject\": \"LN-2026-00632 appraisal support issue\", \"content\": \"Elena,\\n\\nI reviewed the appraisal for 6923 Sharon Rd. We are not able to give value credit for the finished basement area because permits for that improvement were not documented and county records do not support the additional finished square footage.\\n\\nAs reviewed, the appraised support comes in below the contract price if that area is excluded. Please update the file and let us know if you can provide permit documentation or an executed price adjustment.\\n\\nThanks,\\nMegan\", \"cc\": [\"amy.chen@keystonemortgage.com\"], \"parent_id\": \"email_email_e88c593ab4f0\", \"attachments\": {}, \"timestamp\": \"2026-04-14T17:45:00Z\", \"is_read\": false}, {\"email_id\": \"email_email_4a75003c2aa4\", \"folder\": \"INBOX\", \"sender\": \"mtran@carolinaappraisal.com\", \"recipients\": [\"amy.chen@keystonemortgage.com\"], \"subject\": \"RE: Recent sales near the Mitchell property\", \"content\": \"Amy,\\n\\nI reviewed the sales you sent over. I considered them, but I am not making a revision to the report. Two are outside the competitive market area I used, and the other closed after the effective date.\\n\\nThe value conclusion will remain as submitted.\\n\\nMichelle Tran\", \"cc\": [\"elena.marchetti@keystonemortgage.com\"], \"parent_id\": null, \"attachments\": {}, \"timestamp\": \"2026-04-14T17:38:00Z\", \"is_read\": false}, {\"email_id\": \"email_email_e6a87fd77da8\", \"folder\": \"INBOX\", \"sender\": \"megan@carolinahometeam.com\", \"recipients\": [\"natasha.okafor@keystonemortgage.com\"], \"subject\": \"Lauren Mitchell - realistic options?\", \"content\": \"Hi Natasha,\\n\\nLauren filled me in on the appraisal issue and that the value came in short against the contract price on 1937 Nations Ford Rd.\\n\\nSince the appraisal contingency was waived, I need a very honest read from you on what options are actually workable here and how fast we can know. If this is not salvageable with a different structure, I need to understand that now before we run into the contract deadline.\\n\\nCan you let me know whether this looks like:\\n1) borrower bringing in additional cash,\\n2) changing loan structure,\\n3) seller price reduction or credit strategy, or\\n4) not financeable on current terms?\\n\\nI am not asking for guarantees, just the most realistic path and timing so I can advise my client appropriately.\\n\\nThanks,\\nMegan\\nCarolina Home Team\", \"cc\": [\"lauren.mitchell@gmail.com\"], \"parent_id\": null, \"attachments\": {}, \"timestamp\": \"2026-04-14T17:19:00Z\", \"is_read\": false}, {\"email_id\": \"email_email_e88c593ab4f0\", \"folder\": \"INBOX\", \"sender\": \"skessler@unioncountyappraisal.com\", \"recipients\": [\"elena.marchetti@keystonemortgage.com\"], \"subject\": \"Appraisal delivered - 6923 Sharon Rd\", \"content\": \"Hi Elena,\\n\\nThe appraisal for 6923 Sharon Rd is attached and uploaded. During inspection and file review, I noted the finished basement area appears to be an addition not reflected in county records. The reported finished square footage does not match public record, and I could not verify permits for the basement finish.\\n\\nBecause of that, I did not give full gross living area credit to the basement finish in the valuation analysis. I included commentary in the report regarding the county record discrepancy and treatment of the lower level area.\\n\\nLet me know if you obtain permits or other documentation and I can review.\\n\\nThanks,\\nSandra\", \"cc\": [\"amy.chen@keystonemortgage.com\"], \"parent_id\": null, \"attachments\": {}, \"timestamp\": \"2026-04-14T17:10:00Z\", \"is_read\": false}, {\"email_id\": \"email_email_123a53ad2435\", \"folder\": \"INBOX\", \"sender\": \"lauren.mitchell@gmail.com\", \"recipients\": [\"natasha.okafor@keystonemortgage.com\"], \"subject\": \"Re: Appraisal on 1937 Nations Ford\", \"content\": \"Thanks for calling me. I need to be upfront that I do not have another $40,000 to bring in for this house.\\n\\nI already used most of what I had planned for down payment, earnest money, and closing costs. If the loan has to stay the way it is now, I don't think I can make this work.\\n\\nIf there are any other options please let me know asap because I'm really stressed about the contract timing.\", \"cc\": [], \"parent_id\": null, \"attachments\": {}, \"timestamp\": \"2026-04-14T16:50:00Z\", \"is_read\": false}, {\"email_id\": \"email_email_467f00bd7d49\", \"folder\": \"INBOX\", \"sender\": \"lauren.mitchell@gmail.com\", \"recipients\": [\"amy.chen@keystonemortgage.com\"], \"subject\": \"Recent sales near my house\", \"content\": \"Hi Amy,\\n\\nI pulled three recent sales really close to my house that seem a lot more in line with what homes here are actually selling for now. All three are within about 0.2 miles and each one looks roughly $50k higher than the value in the appraisal report.\\n\\nCan you please challenge this appraisal or ask for a review? It doesn't seem right that they used older comps when there are newer sales nearby.\\n\\nThe sales I found are:\\n- 1835 Waverly Ridge Dr -- sold 3/18 for $642,000\\n- 1901 Waverly Ridge Ct -- sold 3/22 for $648,500\\n- 1768 Waverly Ridge Dr -- sold 3/27 for $639,900\\n\\nLet me know what else you need from me.\\n\\nThanks,\\nLauren\", \"cc\": [], \"parent_id\": \"email_email_cbd81b35de81\", \"attachments\": {}, \"timestamp\": \"2026-04-14T14:25:00Z\", \"is_read\": false}, {\"email_id\": \"email_email_cbd81b35de81\", \"folder\": \"INBOX\", \"sender\": \"mtran@carolinaappraisal.com\", \"recipients\": [\"elena.marchetti@keystonemortgage.com\"], \"subject\": \"Mitchell appraisal report\", \"content\": \"Hi Elena,\\n\\nAttached is the completed appraisal report for Lauren Mitchell's refinance.\\n\\nThanks,\\nMichelle Tran\\nCarolina Appraisal Services\", \"cc\": [], \"parent_id\": null, \"attachments\": {}, \"timestamp\": \"2026-04-14T12:19:00Z\", \"is_read\": false}, {\"email_id\": \"email_email_7608e94b0d99\", \"folder\": \"INBOX\", \"sender\": \"b.hensley@tryontitle.com\", \"recipients\": [\"tyler.washington@keystonemortgage.com\"], \"subject\": \"Pham wire not in by cutoff\", \"content\": \"Tyler,\\n\\nWe still have not received lender funds for Destiny Pham. Our bank cutoff for same-day recording was 3:00 PM, and the wire did not hit in time.\\n\\nDocs are fully signed, but we will not be able to record the deed today. We will need to carry this to Monday morning once funds are received.\\n\\nPlease make sure your team and the agents know there will be no recording or seller disbursement today.\\n\\nThanks,\\nBarbara\", \"cc\": [\"cgrayson@graysonlawnc.com\"], \"parent_id\": \"email_email_16c2639d1c07\", \"attachments\": {}, \"timestamp\": \"2026-04-10T18:25:33Z\", \"is_read\": false}, {\"email_id\": \"email_email_16c2639d1c07\", \"folder\": \"INBOX\", \"sender\": \"b.hensley@tryontitle.com\", \"recipients\": [\"tyler.washington@keystonemortgage.com\"], \"subject\": \"Pham docs signed\", \"content\": \"Tyler,\\n\\nBorrower and seller packages are fully signed for the Pham closing. We are wrapped on our side and ready for lender funds and recording this afternoon.\\n\\nBarbara\", \"cc\": [\"cgrayson@graysonlawnc.com\"], \"parent_id\": \"email_email_9469b6f36fc3\", \"attachments\": {}, \"timestamp\": \"2026-04-10T17:40:33Z\", \"is_read\": false}, {\"email_id\": \"email_email_68479af75d6a\", \"folder\": \"INBOX\", \"sender\": \"destiny.pham@gmail.com\", \"recipients\": [\"amy.chen@keystonemortgage.com\"], \"subject\": \"Re: Next steps on the appraisal for your purchase\", \"content\": \"Hi Amy,\\n\\nI talked with my aunt Michelle last night and a family gift may be the only real way I can cover this gap. I don't have that kind of cash on my own.\\n\\nShe has not committed yet and I don't know how much she could do, but I wanted to mention it in case that changes what options we should be looking at.\\n\\nThanks,\\nDestiny\", \"cc\": [\"lauren@queencityhomesrealty.com\"], \"parent_id\": null, \"attachments\": {}, \"timestamp\": \"2026-04-08T18:30:00Z\", \"is_read\": false}], \"next_cursor\": \"MTU\"}"}

# PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL — PREPARED AT THE DIRECTION OF COUNSEL / ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT

**Keystone Mortgage Partners — Security Incident Decision Brief**
**Prepared for:** Robert Calloway, Owner / Licensed Mortgage Broker
**Date:** April 28, 2026
**Distribution:** Robert Calloway; Denise Holloway (CCO); Grace Yamamoto (COO). Keep tight — do not forward.

---

## 1. Bottom line / where my read differs from the March picture

The event you've been carrying as "the ransomware piece" is at least two overlapping problems, and the more serious one is **not** the encryption.

- **Before** the March 20 ransomware, two independent reviews documented **confirmed exports of borrower PII (full/last-4 SSNs and income) out of the LOS using Raj Anand's credentials**, from an out-of-state (Nashville, TN) residential IP during off-hours:
  - **Interim Security Findings Report, dated March 1, 2026** (internal compliance) — four consecutive Feb weekends of off-hours VPN + PII/CSV exports; Raj's account **suspended March 1, 2026**.
  - **Blue Peak Security external audit, April 7, 2026** (Megan Holt) — independently corroborated VPN sessions on Raj's credentials from an out-of-state IP, LOS DB access beyond support scope, and **recurring weekly borrower-data exports over ~6 weeks**.

This changes both of your questions:

- **Pay vs restore:** the person whose Friday-night read you're weighing (Raj) is the **subject** of an active data-exfiltration investigation and controlled the backups. His "restore is expensive" framing cannot be the basis for a pay decision.
- **Borrower notice:** scope has **broadened, not narrowed**, and "unauthorized access cannot be ruled out" has hardened into **confirmed export** for specific, named borrowers.

**Plainly:** the March "ransomware, maybe-accessed" framing understates this. Treat it as a **confirmed insider / credential-based PII exfiltration event with a ransomware event layered on top.**

---

## 2. Pay vs restore

**What the records actually say (not memory):**
- Local backup server encrypted; cloud backup ~72h old (Raj email, 3/20). Ransom note demanded **2 BTC**.
- Restore mechanics (Raj, incident thread, 3/22): best case is restore from the **Tuesday-PM cloud snapshot**; **rebuild infrastructure first, then restore/validate**; "significant data re-entry"; "can't promise LOS integrity till tested."
- So your memory of the restore *mechanics* is accurate: encrypted local backups, ~3-day-old cloud copy, rebuild + validate, manual re-entry for the gap.

**Tradeoffs — and why I read this as restore, not pay:**
1. **Paying does not fix the actual problem.** The core harm is exfiltration that predates and is independent of the encryption. A decryption key does not un-exfiltrate SSNs and does not restore trust in an environment an insider had admin rights to.
2. **Paying does not avoid the rebuild.** Even a clean decrypt leaves a compromised, admin-accessed environment you would still have to rebuild and validate. You would pay 2 BTC *and still do the restore work.*
3. **Sanctions / OFAC exposure.** A ransom payment carries OFAC exposure — the exact question you asked counsel to read. That read is **not back** (see §4). Do not pay before it.
4. **The estimator is conflicted.** Raj scoped both the damage and the "expense" of restoring. Independently validate the restore effort (Blue Peak or an independent IR firm), not on Raj's word.
5. **Open forensic gap.** The March 1 report's action item — *"determine data destination for exported CSV files"* — appears unresolved. Where Raj's exports went is more decision-relevant than the decrypt cost.

**Recommendation:** Proceed on the **restore/rebuild** path; **do not pay**. Commission an independent validation of restore scope and of Raj's backup handling. Hold any payment consideration until counsel's OFAC read.

---

## 3. Borrower-notice posture (current, with specific files)

**Where Denise's 3/20 plan stands:** notice drafts were queued as a parallel track (Denise → Sloane/Robert, 3/20 19:20); Raj never produced a clean file-level exposure list; SAR flagged as "probably on the table." That plan was never closed out — but the facts under it have moved.

**Confirmed PII exports (CSV incl. SSN + income) — LOS Audit Extract + Blue Peak, Feb 2026:**
- **LN-2026-00184 — Marisol Reyes** (SSN …4421) — full SSN + income exported
- **LN-2026-00211 — Tyler Morgan** (…7719) — SSN last4 + income
- **LN-2026-00237 — Alicia Bennett** (…1183)
- **LN-2026-00244 — Kevin Durham** (…5608)
- **Plus a 38-row "ALL-PIPELINE" bulk export (2/24)** = many additional borrowers whose pipeline data left the environment. *The named list must be reconstructed from that export.*

**Separate access exposures feeding the SAME notice analysis** (you said anything feeding borrower notice counts, even from a separate workstream):
- **Leo Park (intern), 3/17–3/30:** 34+ borrower files opened "not assigned," repeated fixation on **LN-2026-00554**, weekend/after-hours (viewing; export not confirmed) — Leo Park Access Review, 3/31.
- **Evan Mercer (post-termination LOS access):** opened **LN-2025-00002, LN-2025-00007, LN-2026-00009** after separation; offboarding failed to revoke LOS access; poaching/contact-pull concern raised.
- **Marcus (mailbox):** 4 forwards to a personal address + bulk pipeline/loan-summary downloads; **LN-2026-00608** contact material exported.
- **Ransomware entry** via phishing of Tyler (processor), 3/20; **Keisha** phishing / UWM restriction + password reuse.

**SAR:** with confirmed insider PII exfiltration (not just a ransom demand), the FinCEN SAR question is more live than in March. Counsel's call; nothing filed on record.

**Net:** scope is wider and the exfiltration question is largely answered in the affirmative for named individuals. This **strengthens** the borrower-notification obligation (GLBA Safeguards/notice + NC and likely multi-state breach-notice laws) relative to the March "cannot rule out" posture.

---

## 4. Legal / what is still open (answering "has anything shifted?")

- **Outside cyber counsel** = Megan Sloane, Ward Barrett Law — engaged 3/20 for privileged guidance incl. OFAC/sanctions on ransom, privilege preservation, notice timing, and SAR.
- **Nothing has come back in writing.** No email from Sloane / Ward Barrett is on file; her formal sanctions/privilege read and her sign-off on the notice-prep parallel track both appear **still outstanding**. Confirm status verbally, but on paper it is open.
- **What counsel still needs before you decide:** (i) the reconciled fact set in §1–3 (being sent); (ii) the reconstructed borrower list from the 2/24 bulk export; (iii) the unresolved "where did the exports go" answer; (iv) confirmation of preservation across LOS logs, mailboxes, and export audit trails.
- **Governance flag you should hear directly:** Grace has stated (Slack, ~4/4) she "signed off on access being too broad on Raj's side." That is an internal control failure and makes Grace conflicted as an owner of the Raj workstream — worth walling off in how the review is staffed.

---

## 5. Decisions I'm asking you to make

1. Endorse **restore/rebuild**; **no ransom payment** pending counsel's OFAC read.
2. Authorize **independent** validation of restore scope + Raj's backup handling (not Raj).
3. Direct counsel to give the **notice trigger/timing** and **SAR** read on the *confirmed-exfiltration* facts, and reconstruct the 2/24 bulk-export borrower list.
4. Keep the **Raj workstream independent of Grace** given her stated conflict.
5. Confirm all logs / mailboxes / exports remain under **preservation hold**.

---

*Sources: Interim Security Findings Report (3/1/26); Blue Peak Security audit email (4/7/26) and supporting evidence (vpn_access_log_feb.pdf, los_audit_extract_offhours.pdf, raj_anand_access_history.pdf); Leo Park Access Review (3/31/26); privileged email thread Denise Holloway ↔ Megan Sloane (3/20/26); incident command Slack threads (#general, #it-support). Counsel correspondence resides in the privileged email thread and should be preserved there.*

OUR CURRENT POSTURE:

Done, Robert. Here's where it lands — and I'll say the hard part first, because it changes your decision.

## The thing you need to hear plainly
The picture you've been operating on ("ransomware, maybe some data touched, Raj says restore is a lift") **understates this.** Going to the primary records, the more serious problem isn't the encryption at all. Two independent reviews — our own **Interim Security Findings (March 1)** and **Blue Peak's external audit (April 7)** — document **confirmed exports of borrower PII, including full/last-4 SSNs and income, out of the LOS on Raj Anand's credentials**, off-hours, from a Nashville, TN IP, across four+ February sessions plus a 38-row bulk pipeline export. His account was suspended March 1 — *before* the March 20 ransomware. **Raj, whose restore read you're weighing, is the subject of the investigation and controlled the backups.**

## Pay vs restore
Your memory of the *mechanics* is accurate — the records confirm it: local backups encrypted, cloud copy ~72h old (Tuesday PM), rebuild-then-restore-then-validate, significant manual re-entry for the gap. But the tradeoff isn't "expensive restore, so maybe pay." My read is **restore/rebuild, do not pay**, because:
- Paying doesn't un-exfiltrate SSNs and doesn't restore trust in an admin-compromised environment.
- Paying doesn't even avoid the rebuild — you'd pay 2 BTC *and still* rebuild/validate.
- OFAC/sanctions exposure — the exact read you asked counsel for, still not back.
- The cost estimate came from a conflicted subject. Validate it independently, not on Raj's word. And the March 1 action item "determine where the exported CSVs went" is still open — that matters more than the decrypt cost.

## Borrower-notice posture
Scope has **broadened, not narrowed**, and "can't rule out access" is now "**confirmed export**" for named files: **LN-2026-00184 (Reyes), -00211 (Morgan), -00237 (Bennett), -00244 (Durham)**, plus the 2/24 bulk export (list still to be reconstructed). Feeding the same notice population from other workstreams: **Leo Park** (34+ unassigned files viewed, 3/17–3/30), **Evan Mercer** post-termination access (LN-2025-00002/-00007, LN-2026-00009), and the **Marcus mailbox** forwards (incl. LN-2026-00608). SAR is more live now, not less. Denise's parallel notice-prep track was queued but never closed out.

## Legal — has anything shifted?
On paper, **no** — and that's the point. There's **no written response from Megan Sloane / Ward Barrett on file**. Her OFAC/sanctions read, privilege posture, notice timing, and SAR guidance are all still outstanding. Confirm with her verbally, but nothing has come back. (Governance flag: Grace stated she signed off on Raj's access being too broad — she's conflicted on that workstream.)

## What I did
1. **Decision brief** → `audit/incident_response_2026/decision_brief_2026-04-28.md`, alongside the forensic evidence.
2. **Emailed outside counsel** (Sloane, cc Denise), privileged, with the reconciled facts and the five open questions gating your decision.
3. **Leadership status** posted to the Robert/Grace/Denise channel — contained, not pushed wider.
4. **Formal note** logged in the CRM engagement log (measured; SSNs omitted for data minimization).

**Decisions waiting on you:** endorse restore/no-pay pending OFAC read; authorize independent restore validation; direct counsel to rule on notice/SAR against the confirmed-exfiltration facts and reconstruct the bulk-export list; wall the Raj workstream off from Grace; confirm the preservation hold.
